subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — FinSolve
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex@datawise.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — FinSolve

Hi Alex (and Priya, thanks for joining briefly),

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap so we have a shared view and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you called out:
- Production latency spikes at peak traffic (affects search ranking updates)
- Cost unpredictability with on-demand GPUs and multi-tenant inference endpoints
- Data isolation and auditability requirements for regulated customers

Current stack & footprint (what you told us)
- Models: mix of open models (LLM-embed-v2) for embeddings, and a small Llama-variant for reranking
- Infra: AWS EKS fronted by ALBs, model pods on spot GPU nodes today; fallback to CPU is slow
- Traffic: ~100–140 TPS peak for embeddings during batch windows; average 25–30 TPS
- KV/prefix caching is partial (in-house)

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit
- Predictable throughput: sustained 120 TPS for embeddings with 95th pct latency < 150ms
- Isolation: no co-tenant access to inference workloads or logs; dedicated GPU pool
- Autoscale/burst: ability to absorb 2x peak for short bursts without dropped requests
- Security: SOC 2 + contract-level access controls

Proposed initial config (back-of-envelope)
- Dedicated GPU pool (N x A100-sim) sized for 120 TPS sustained with room for 2x burst; see attached estimate
- Autoscaling policy: reserved baseline + burst capacity via warm standby nodes; configurable cooldowns
- Observability: token-level latency breakdown and per-model dashboards in Redwood Console

Next steps
1) Share sizing worksheet (attached) — confirm traffic patterns and seq lengths so we can firm estimates
2) Schedule infra deep-dive with your SREs (Aditya & Vanessa can join) — propose Tue or Wed next week
3) Legal/Proc: we'll send a mutual action plan and draft SOW for internal review (Priya looped)
4) Security: we shared an SOC2 snapshot and can provide more artifacts on request

Attachments: Dedicated-Capacity-Estimate.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the infra deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
On Thu, Apr 2, 2026 at 15:00 Alex Turner <alex@datawise.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Marissa — quick notes in case they help ahead of our call.
> 
> Alex

From: Alex Turner <alex@datawise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsolve.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — FinSolve

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — that aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications and additions from our side:

- Traffic: embeddings peak is closer to 125–140 TPS during end-of-day batch jobs; bursts can briefly hit ~270 TPS for 2–5 minutes during promos
- Sequence lengths: most embeddings requests are short (avg 64 tokens) but reranker inputs can be 512–1,024 tokens on longer queries
- Caching: we rely on an in-house Redis prefix cache but miss rate is high for new queries
- Security/compliance: we are SOC2 Type II in scope but procurement will want audit logs and VPC isolation; will need KMS integration for CMKs

Attachments: vendor-security-questionnaire.pdf (procurement asked for this)

Can you confirm whether your Dedicated offering supports:
1) Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key)
2) Private VPC peering and egress control
3) SLA for 99.9% inference uptime for reserved pools

Also — price band and whether a pilot with committed capacity is possible (we'd like a 6–8 week pilot window). Priya will own procurement/contract questions from here.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Senior Platform Engineer, Datawise (FinSolve partner)
alex@datawise.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex@datawise.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsolve.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — FinSolve

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great context — thanks. Quick answers to your questions and what we'll bring to procurement: 

1) Customer-managed KMS: yes, Redwood Private/Dedicated supports BYOK with CMK integration and we can provide HSM/KMS attestations
2) Private VPC: yes — we support VPC peering and strict egress controls for Private deployments; for Hosted Dedicated we offer private network options and dedicated tenancy
3) SLA: we offer SLA-backed reserved pools; exact numbers and credits will be in the SOW (we can target 99.9% inference uptime for reserved pools)

Pilot: we commonly do a 6–8 week pilot with reserved minimums; we can draft a pilot MOP (scope, sizing, success criteria).

Requested next items from us:
- Firm up typical sequence lengths/percentiles and confirm burst patterns (timestamps if possible) — this will change the kernel/memory sizing
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (60–90m) with your infra team — Vanessa and Aditya available Tue/Wed next week (Tue 10–12 or Wed 1–3 PT)
- We'll share a draft MSA/SOW + pilot terms for Priya to review (expect in 48 hours)

Attaching: Dedicated-Capacity-Estimate.xlsx (updated with escrows for 2x burst), mutual-action-plan.docx, SOC2-snapshot.pdf. HubSpot deal link included in the sheet.

If that all looks good I'll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Happy to join the deep-dive. For the technical session we'll prepare:
